_doc: Which harnesses follow the simulation clock on their own, and which may receive timer turns (docs/adapters.md, "Timer turns"). native_scheduler: whether the harness's own cron or timer fires on the world's simulation clock in a trial. Every adapter runs the harness turn by turn with no gateway, and nothing runs between turns, so none does: an agent's own schedule fires only through world timers, which the runner delivers as timer turns. timer_turns: certified when tests/timer-turn-adapters.test.ts proves the adapter answers a timer turn in the session of the turn that set the timer; the runner refuses a [clock] timers task on any other harness (HE-PREREG-009).

claude-code.native_scheduler: none: Claude Code has no scheduler of its own in headless -p turns

codex.native_scheduler: none: codex exec runs one turn and exits

openclaw.native_scheduler: not driven: OpenClaw's cron runs in its gateway, which the adapter does not start (agent --local per turn)
openclaw.note: a model answer of NO_REPLY is OpenClaw's own silent reply; under agent --local OpenClaw then reports an empty response and the adapter exits 2, so the runner's quiet word is NOTHING_TO_SAY

hermes.native_scheduler: not driven: Hermes's cron runs in its gateway, which the adapter does not start (chat --oneshot per turn)

qm.native_scheduler: not driven: QM's scheduled work runs on core's wall clock
qm.reason: serve cannot register the world MCP server at the pinned commit (QM refuses private network addresses); QM added PRIVATE_NETWORK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS in 198faa2b6 (yc-software/qm#3206), so certifying QM needs a pin at or after it
